newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Radical Chechen guerrilla chief critically hurt.
newsitem.headline: Radical Chechen guerrilla chief critically hurt.

text.p: Radical Chechen guerrilla commander Salman Raduyev, one of Russia's most wanted men, has been critically injured in an assassination attempt, an aide said on Friday.
Sultan Miyev, Raduyev's military consultant, told Reuters in the Chechen capital Grozny that Raduyev's car had been blown up early on Wednesday on a road outside the city.
"He is very seriously injured. He underwent an operation but it was not successful. He is in critical condition in hospital," Miyev said.
Raduyev, who led a bloody armed raid in the Russian region of Dagestan bordering Chechnya last January, was reported killed in an ambush last year.
He later resurfaced, saying he had been seriously hurt but had undergone plastic surgery in Germany. His face was barely recognisable.

Miyev blamed Russian forces for Wednesday's incident, near the town of Urus-Martan about 20 km (12 miles) from Grozny, and promised revenge attacks. The Chechens frequently blame Russian agents provocateurs for trouble in their Caucasus region.
"I want to say as military consultant to Raduyev's army that on April 21 or 22 there will be a revenge blow in Russia. The Russians will find out for themselves when and in what towns," he said.

He promised one attack to avenge Raduyev and one to avenge former Chechen President Dzhokhar Dudayev, believed killed in a Russian rocket attack last April 20 during the 20-month conflict over Chechnya's independence drive.

Radayev is wanted by Russian police for masterminding the Dagestan raid. Movladi Udugov, first deputy prime minister in the rebel region, was quoted by Itar-Tass news agency as saying that he had no information about an assassination attempt.
Raduyev has vowed several times to launch attacks in Russia but none has materialised.
It is not clear how many armed supporters he has, although Chechnya, where rebels fought a 21-month war with Russian troops sent to crush an independence bid, is still awash with weapons.

Russia and Chechnya stopped fighting under a ceasefire signed last August and Russia pulled all its forces out, but peace talks are bogged down over Chechnya's political status. Chechnya wants full independence but Russia rules this out.
